channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Nidec Shares Plunge After Auditor Withholds Opinion on Earnings
item.description: Nidec Corp. shares dropped as much as 20% in Tokyo after the Japanese motor maker’s auditor declined to give an opinion on its long-awaited full-year results, fueling caution over the scandal-hit company.
item.dc:creator: Aya Wagatsuma and Alice French

item.title: South Korea’s Export Growth Extends Rally as Chip Boom Rolls on
item.description: South Korea’s exports extended their strong growth in September as global demand for artificial intelligence continued to power semiconductor shipments, raising expectations that the trade-dependent economy will remain resilient despite higher interest rates.
item.dc:creator: Heesu Lee

item.title: Micron Gives Bullish Forecast, Warns on Margins
item.description: Micron Technology Inc. gave an upbeat forecast for the current quarter, fueled by the AI building frenzy, though the chipmaker warned that rising compensation would weigh on profit margins. Bloomberg Intelligence's Jake Silverman has more. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Fed’s Kashkari Says AI Not Only Driver of US Economic Growth
item.description: Federal Reserve Bank of Minneapolis President Neel Kashkari said he was skeptical of the argument that the US economy is shrinking but for a boom in construction related to artificial intelligence.
item.dc:creator: Laura Curtis

item.title: Morocco Used Spyware on Activists, Journalists, Report Says
item.description: Moroccan authorities have used spyware for years against critics in the country and overseas, including French and Spanish politicians, according to a new report from Amnesty International, which is based on leaked documents and testimony from a former Moroccan intelligence official.
item.dc:creator: Ryan Gallagher

item.title: September Market Recap & Micron’s AI Boom
item.description: The Close brings you the latest news and analysis leading up to the final minutes and seconds before and after the closing bell on Wall Street. Today's guests are BlackRock Head of Model Portfolio Solutions, Americas Michael Gates, Robinhood Markets Chairman & CEO Vlad Tenev, University of Michigan Professor of Economics and Public Policy Betsey Stevenson, Morgan Stanley Investment Management Head of Global Real Assets Lauren Hochfelder, Janus Henderson Head of Americas Equities Marc Pinto, Gabelli Research Analyst & Portfolio Manager Hendi Susanto, Redpoint Ventures Managing Director Erica Brescia, VSORA Chair Sandra Rivera, JPMorgan Asset Management Global Alternatives Strategist Aaron Mulvihill, Seaport Research Partners Senior Analyst David Joyce, & Next Legacy Managing Partner Ryan Nece. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Next Legacy’s Ryan Nece on the Rise of Athlete Investing
item.description: Ryan Nece joins the program to talk about how he thinks about investing after football and where he is deploying capital now. Nece discusses whether he is putting all of his money into AI, setting up a conversation about current investment priorities and how athletes can approach venture investing after their playing careers. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Redpoint Ventures’ Brescia on Micron Q4 & AI Outlook
item.description: Micron delivered results that beat already elevated expectations, with fourth-quarter numbers exceeding guidance and first-quarter outlook also coming in ahead of estimates. Erica Brescia, Managing Director at Redpoint Ventures and Former COO at GitHub, whether the explosive growth in the sector can continue. She speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Kreiz a Good Choice for Paramount, Seaport's Joyce Says
item.description: Seaport Research Partners Senior Analyst David Joyce reacts to Ynon Kreiz joining Paramount Skydance as co-CEO of the merged company after the completion of the pending $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery. Joyce speaks on "Bloomberg The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Morgan Stanley’s Hochfelder: Industrials Is Next Growth Area
item.description: Lauren Hochfelder, Head of Global Real Assets at Morgan Stanley, says commercial real estate may be at an appealing turning point after a prolonged correction. She notes the sector is now more than four years into what she describes as the longest correction in over 30 years, with prices still down more than 20% and trading below replacement cost for the first time since the global financial crisis. She speaks with Romaine Bostick & Emily Graffeo on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: HPE Boosts Forecast on Positive Networking Outlook
item.description:
Hewlett Packard Enterprise Co. boosted its networking revenue forecast and announced a $1.2 billion order from cloud company Vultr, giving fresh signals that it’s benefiting from the AI build-out.
The company, which expanded its networking business by acquiring Juniper Networks last year, now expects that segment to range from the high teens to the low 20s in percentage sales growth during fiscal 2027. The company also gave a longer-range sales outlook in the high teens, with an operating margin target of as much as the high 20s. For more, we speak with Marie Myers, Chief Financial Officer at HPE. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: The Key Takeaways From Micron's Better-Than-Expected Forecast
item.description: Hendi Susanto, a research analyst and portfolio manager at Gabelli, reacts to Micron Technology giving a sales forecast for the current quarter that shattered estimates after the AI building frenzy fueled unprecedented demand. He speaks on "Bloomberg The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Micron Forecast Tops Estimates on Booming AI Memory Demand
item.description: Micron Technology Inc., the largest US maker of memory chips, gave a sales forecast for the current quarter that shattered estimates after the AI building frenzy fueled unprecedented demand. Revenue will be about $61.5 billion in the fiscal first quarter, which runs through November, the company said in a statement Wednesday. Analysts estimated $56.8 billion on average. Excluding some items, profit will be about $38.15 a share, compared with a projection of $36.02. We get reaction from Jake Silverman, Bloomberg Intelligence Semiconductor Analyst. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Former NY Governor Cuomo Buys $9.6 Million Hamptons Estate
item.description: Former New York Governor Andrew Cuomo purchased a roughly seven-acre estate on the south shore of Long Island for $9.6 million, according to a spokesperson and property records.
item.dc:creator: Cameron Fozi and Laura Nahmias

item.title: Kalshi Finalizing New Funding at $40 Billion Value Ahead of IPO
item.description: Kalshi Inc. is finalizing a new financing round that would value the prediction market platform at around $40 billion, according to people familiar with the matter. The deal is expected to be the startup’s last round before an initial public offering, which is anticipated as soon as next year, the people said.
item.dc:creator: Natasha Mascarenhas and Denitsa Tsekova

item.title: Ackman on AI & IPOs, Climate Costs, Paramount's Debt Raise
item.description: A weekly, midday program that delivers high-impact, editorially driven coverage of the most important corporate transactions shaping the global market. Today's guests: Pershing Square CEO & Founder Bill Ackman, Pulse Fund Founder & Managing Partner Tenzin Seldon, EQT Partner, Head of AI Infrastructure Jan Vesely, BCG Global Head of Sustainable Investing Vinay Shandal, and JPMorgan Private Bank Global Head of Alternative Investments Kristin Kallergis Rowland. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Micron Gives Bullish Forecast, Even as Pay Raises Crimp Margins
item.description: Micron Technology Inc. gave an upbeat forecast for the current quarter, fueled by the AI building frenzy, though the chipmaker warned that rising compensation would weigh on profit margins.
item.dc:creator: Dina Bass

item.title: Amazon Nuke Deal to Help Expand Constellation Maryland Site
item.description: Amazon.com Inc. has agreed to purchase 690 megawatts of power from Constellation Energy Corp. in a deal that will help the biggest US nuclear operator boost capacity at the only reactors in Maryland.
item.dc:creator: Will Wade

item.title: Google Grapples With Employee Skepticism About New Gemini 4
item.description: Alphabet Inc.’s Google has begun rolling out Gemini 4 Argon, its long-awaited flagship artificial intelligence model, but the company is grappling with internal skepticism over how well it performs in key areas, such as coding.
item.dc:creator: Julia Love and Davey Alba

item.title: Bitcoin Rides Risk Roller Coaster as Speculative Bets Wind Down
item.description: Bitcoin enjoyed a brief respite along with other risk assets such as stocks amid the expectation that another rate hike is unlikely next month.
item.dc:creator: David Pan
